translation: Fera wrote that letter.
comment: Active: meN- with the agent before any auxiliary. The source bases the example on Sneddon 1996:xxiii.

translation: That letter was written by Fera.
comment: di- passive; the agent, if any, is an oleh phrase. The source bases the example on Sneddon 1996:xxiii.

translation: I wrote that letter.
comment: Bare passive: no prefix, agent immediately preverbal. The source bases the example on Sneddon 1996:xxiii.

primaryText: Buku yang Wati tulis ada di atas meja itu.
translation: The book that Wati wrote is on the table.
comment: Object extraction requires the verb without meN-. The source cites (SI; Cole & Hermon 2005:67).

primaryText: Buku yang Wati men-ulis ada di atas meja itu.
comment: The overt Voice yields the ordering paradox of (57). The source cites (SI; Cole & Hermon 2005:67).

primaryText: Kami tidak akan mem-baca buku ini.
translation: We will not read this book.
comment: Agent subjects precede the auxiliaries in the active. The source cites (SI; Cole et al. 2008:1512).

primaryText: Tidak akan kami mem-baca buku ini.
comment: An active agent cannot follow the auxiliaries. The source cites (SI; Cole et al. 2008:1512).

primaryText: Buku ini tidak akan kami baca.
translation: We will not read this book.
comment: Bare passive agents are low, after the auxiliaries. The source cites (SI; Cole & Hermon 2005:62–63).

primaryText: Siapa-kah yang telah mem-baca buku itu?
translation: Who has read the book?
comment: Subject extraction from the active keeps meN-. The source cites (SM; Soh 1998:297).

translation: clothes that Ali isn't washing
comment: Object extraction across a high, pre-auxiliary agent, only without meN-. The source cites (SM; Keenan 1972:183–84).
The source cites (SM; Keenan 1972:183–84).

primaryText: Kepada Ani, Hasan meng-irim-kan surat itu.
translation: To Ani, Hasan sent the letter.
comment: PP extraction from the active keeps meN-: the PP is a further specifier of VoiceP. The source cites (Chung 1976a:78).

translation: To whom were those flowers given?
comment: The source cites (Chung 1976b:82).

primaryText: Kepada siapa bunga itu kau beri-kan?
translation: To whom did you give those flowers?
comment: PP extraction from the bare passive. The source cites (Chung 1976b:82).

translation: This book, Badu has read.
comment: Object topicalization: the theme and the agent move out of VoiceP order-preservingly, Voice null. The source cites (SI; Voskuil 2000:199, Musgrave 2001:60).
The source cites (SI; Voskuil 2000:199, Musgrave 2001:60).

primaryText: Siapa yang pintu itu akan buka?
translation: Who will the door be opened by?
comment: Bare-passive agent extraction: the theme precedes the agent at VoiceP but would follow it at CP. The source gives the translation as intended. The source cites (SI; based on Vamarasi 1999:55).

translation: S/he ties the boat.
comment: Desa active with the short prefix. Suak Mansi Desa (West Bornean Malayic, undescribed before the paper) has no Glottolog code; the Western Malayic Dayak subgroup's is used.

translation: S/he ties the boat.
comment: Desa active with the long prefix, in free variation with (5) N-.

primaryText: Makanan mau' di-kirim (oleh uma'-ku) ke Meliau.
translation: Food will be sent to Meliau (by my mother).
comment: Desa di- passive.

translation: I touch the table.
comment: Desa bare passive.
The bare passive allows neither active prefix: with the active v the agent would go unlicensed.

translation: S/he is bringing wood.

comment: di- needs adjacency to v, which the low agent breaks.

translation: My mother makes chicken.

comment: Without an agent, Voice is adjacent to the passive v and must be di-.

translation: The book was written.

primaryText: Buku yetn lelaki yetn tongah tulis.
comment: A bare-passive agent cannot precede the auxiliaries; the row records the agent as the pre-auxiliary nominal with the theme initial, a surface no derivation yields.

primaryText: Buku yetn tongah lelaki yetn tulis.
translation: The man is writing the book.
Who tied the boat?
comment: Subject extraction from the active; T licenses the extracted agent in situ.

translation: Who took my basket?

primaryText: Opai yang tau' di-tanam di taman?
translation: What can be planted in the field?
comment: Subject extraction from the di- passive.

translation: It's this book that my father bought.
comment: Object extraction keeps N- and has the agent immediately preverbal.
me- would need adjacency to v, and Voice must be null.

translation: What isn't s/he looking for?
comment: The agent follows the auxiliaries in Desa object extraction.
Under nominal extraction Desa T licenses in situ and attracts nothing to Spec,TP.

primaryText: Di oni inya m-oli beju to?
translation: Where did s/he buy this shirt?
comment: PP extraction is insensitive to voice.

primaryText: Di oni inya mem-oli beju to?
translation: Where did s/he buy this shirt?

primaryText: Di oni beju to di-beli oleh inya?
translation: Where was this shirt bought by him/her?

primaryText: Aku nge-liet lelaki yang di-ikat tali yetn.
comment: Agent extraction with the passive v: the agent would Ā-move out of its licensing position in Spec,vP.

primaryText: Aku nge-liet lelaki yang ng-ikat tali yetn.
translation: I saw the man that tied the rope.

primaryText: Aku nge-liet lelaki yang meng-ikat tali yetn.
translation: I saw the man that tied the rope.
The child is reading a book.
comment: Jakarta Indonesian (Tjung 2006): the optional N- realizes Voice. The source cites (Tjung 2006:22–24).

translation: The child is reading a book.
comment: The bare active. The source cites (Tjung 2006:22–24).

translation: Who is reading a book?
comment: The source cites (Tjung 2006:22–24).

translation: Who is reading a book?
comment: The source cites (Tjung 2006:22–24).
N- on Voice blocks object extraction, as meN- does in the standard languages. The source cites (Tjung 2006:22–24).

translation: What is the child reading?
comment: The source cites (Tjung 2006:22–24).

primaryText: Buku yang gua nggak lagi baca mahal.
translation: The book that I am not reading is expensive.
comment: The agent precedes the auxiliaries: object extraction, not a bare passive. The source cites (Tjung 2006:25).

translation: What did you plant?
comment: Kuching Malay, Glottolog's Sarawak Malay (sara1351): object extraction across an N- or bare active, N- realizing v. The source cites (Cole et al. 2008:1548–49).

translation: What did you plant?
comment: Kuching Malay, Glottolog's Sarawak Malay (sara1351): object extraction across an N- or bare active, N- realizing v. The source cites (Cole et al. 2008:1548–49).

translation: Father called his son.
comment: Polite Madurese (Jeoung 2017): Voice realizes N- next to the active v.

translation: The son was called by father.
Father called his son.
comment: The polite register has a bare passive: Voice has a null allomorph.

translation: Ali called his child.
comment: Familiar Madurese.

translation: The child was called by Ali.
I called his child.
comment: No bare passive: familiar Voice has no null allomorph and its overt prefix cannot affix across the agent. The source gives the translation as intended.

primaryText: Buku panekah se ramah ampon bacah.
translation: It's that book that father read.
comment: Object extraction in the polite register, the agent before the auxiliary.

primaryText: Buku panekah se ramah ampon m-acah.
Buku jiyah se David la bacah.
translation: It's that book that David read.
comment: No object extraction in the familiar register. The source gives the translation as intended.

primaryText: Buku jiyah se David la m-acah.
translation: It's that book that David read.
comment: The source gives the translation as intended.
